text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: A law-and-order policy action (laws to crack down on domestic violence); while the topic is morally charged, the statement itself is programmatic with no explicit moral vocabulary.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: Programme rollout for fruit and vegetable promotion; administrative.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: Annual reporting requirement; governance administration.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Instrumental rationale for talking therapies (recovery and return to work); technical.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: Resource reallocation for whānau development; programmatic.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: Parental leave design; 'choice' is presented as a policy feature, not an ethical claim.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: 'Wise use of public dollars' expresses fiscal prudence, an administrative value, not moral ethics per the codebook.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: Debt-per-household arithmetic; purely descriptive fiscal content.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: Maintaining the Defence Forces' 'proud reputation' in peacekeeping is about prestige; 'proud' is mildly evaluative but the sentence invokes no ethical standard, so coded 0 (borderline).

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Explicitly invokes a 'fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians' — fairness, respect and rights are ethical concepts listed in marker 1 of the clarification.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: 'Eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system' deploys equality/inequality, a key ethical concept (marker 1), as an explicit normative target.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Describes a statutory requirement to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid; the 'must' reflects legal obligation and the text makes no moralized claim about aid's purpose.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: Descriptive account of an MP introducing a housing bill; no evaluative or moral language.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: Spending commitment for aged care beds; programmatic.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Community policing reform; 'spirit of genuine partnership' is organizational aspiration, not an explicit ethical concept.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Cutting government 'waste' is an efficiency/fiscal pledge; 'waste' here is not a moral category like corruption.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: 'Best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old' is a superlative national aspiration without ethical vocabulary; a generic commitment.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Ending an administrative entitlement (ministerial cars); no moral framing in the text.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: The rhetorical attack 'If you can't trust Labour and National... what on earth can you trust them on', amplified by the emotive 'poisoned baby milk', appeals to honesty/trustworthiness as civic virtues, fitting the definition's personal/civic virtues criterion.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: Parliamentary procedure for selecting bills; administrative.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: Commemorating the Easter Rising 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' deploys honour/respect language and patriotic commemoration, matching marker 3 (patriotism); mild but explicit.

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration policy justified by economic needs; 'sensible' is mild pragmatic evaluation, not moral terminology.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: 'Accountability framework' is a technocratic governance term in education management; no ethical appeal.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: 'The victory of free nations in the War on Terror' invokes freedom/liberty as a normative ideal and frames geopolitics as a moral contest, going beyond descriptive strategy; borderline but value-laden.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: Debate procedure; administrative.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: Fisheries compliance and enforcement; 'poachers' is a standard label for rule violators, and the appeal is to policing the system rather than to ethical standards.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: Jobs-created record; descriptive.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: Generic constitutional stability commitment; no moral vocabulary.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: 'Dysfunctional' is a performance evaluation of an agency; technocratic critique, not moral judgment.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: Technical critique of waste-processing scale and traffic impacts; no normative language.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Decarbonized economy aspiration; economic/environmental framing without moral terms.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: Business competitiveness goal; purely economic.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: 'A fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned' explicitly deploys fairness (marker 1) plus a normative claim about what regions ought to receive.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Sport participation and volunteering statistics; descriptive.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognition of Māori enterprise's economic contribution; descriptive, with no explicit ethical terminology.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A commitment to implement the Military Covenant; although the covenant connotes obligation, the text itself deploys no explicit moral vocabulary and reads as a policy implementation pledge.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Critiques a party-funding rule as disadvantaging smaller parties, but does so descriptively ('acts against', 'could be seen as') without invoking fairness or equality explicitly.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: 'Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means' explicitly invokes the ethical concept of fairness (marker 1) to morally indict an opponent.

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: Programme development (parent education); administrative.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: Trade enforcement policy on anti-dumping; no moral vocabulary.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: 'Obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions' refers to institutional/treaty obligations; the framing is organizational rather than a moral duty appeal.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: Descriptive critique of administrative delays and litigation frequency; technical process language with no moral terminology.
